title: GeoLocator Data Package: Barred Warblers from Czechia

contributors.title: Adamik, Peter
contributors.organization: Palacký University Olomouc, Museum of Natural History

description:
This Geolocator Data Package contains the analyzed data (using GeoPressureR) for two Barred Warblers tracked from Czechia. This data has been published here: Migration and daily flight activity patterns in the barred warbler Curruca nisoria over the annual cycle.

If you would like to use the data, please contact Joanna Wong (joanna.wong@vogelwarte.ch)
bibliographicCitation:
Wong J, Adamik P, Bažant M, Hahn S (2025). “GeoLocator Data Package:
Barred Warblers from Czechia.” doi:10.5281/zenodo.17367319

schema.name: tags
schema.title: Tags
schema.description:
`tags.csv` is a [tabular data](https://datapackage.org/standard/glossary/#tabular-data) resource from a GeoLocator Data Package. Each tag listed in this table is assumed to have been deployed only once on a single bird. This table contains information about the device, the deployment, and the equipped bird. Data collected on the bird that may change over time (e.g., `age_class`) should be provided in the [`observations`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/observations) table.

Additional data can be provided by following the [Movebank tag attribute dictionary](https://www.movebank.org/cms/movebank-content/movebank-attribute-dictionary#tag_attributes) and [Movebank deployment attribute dictionary](https://www.movebank.org/cms/movebank-content/movebank-attribute-dictionary#deployment_attributes).

 **Example:** [`tags.csv`](https://github.com/GeoPressure/GeoLocator-DP/blob/main/example/tags.csv)

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag.

fields.name: datapackage_id
fields.description: Optional identifier of the data package for this tag, typically corresponding to the `datapackage.id`. This field is mostly used when [merging multiple data packages](https://geopressure.org/GeoLocatoR/reference/merge_gldp.html).

fields.name: ring_number
fields.description: Ring number associated with the tagged bird. This value is not unique at table level because the same bird can receive multiple tag deployments (`tag_id`).

fields.name: scientific_name
fields.description: Scientific name of the tagged species.

fields.name: manufacturer
fields.description: The company or person that produced the tag. When appropriate, please use the terms `'Swiss Ornithological Institute'`, `'Migrate Technology Limited'`, `'Lund University'`, `'British Antarctic Survey'`, or `'PresTag'`.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Model/design/version of the tag. Any device specification that can identify it.

fields.name: firmware
fields.description: The tag firmware and version used during the deployment.

fields.name: weight
fields.description: Weight of the device with harness. Expressed in grams.

fields.name: attachment_type
fields.description: The way a tag is attached to an animal. Use values from the [Movebank `attachment type` concept](https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/MVB/current/MVB000052) if possible. Assumed to be `harness` if not provided. You can also provide the material used.

fields.name: readout_method
fields.description: The way the data are received from the tag. Use values from the [Movebank `tag readout method` concept](https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/MVB/current/MVB000188/) if possible. Assumed to be `tag-retrieval` if not provided.

fields.name: tag_comments
fields.description: Comments or notes about the tag, deployment, or animal. Use this field to provide additional information that does not fit in other fields, such as data-quality issues, deployment/retrieval details, or analysis notes (e.g., labeling effort, quality checks, or issues encountered).

schema.name: observations
schema.title: observations
schema.description:
`observations.csv` is a [tabular data](https://datapackage.org/standard/glossary/#tabular-data) resource from a GeoLocator Data Package containing relevant [events](http://rs.tdwg.org/dwc/terms/Event) (datetime and location) that typically happen in the field and provide important information for analysis. These observations should include at least equipment and, when appropriate, retrieval events, as well as ringing controls or direct sightings.

{:.alert .alert-info}
You can think of `observations` as your log entries in your ringing book.

An observation is described at minimum by `datetime`, location (`latitude` and `longitude`), `ring_number`, and `observation_type` (e.g., equipment, retrieval, or capture). In addition, `sex` and `age_class` are required (use `U` for unknown `sex` and `0` for unknown `age_class`).

Also include ringing events for any control group (i.e., birds ringed but not equipped with a tag).

 **Example:** [`observations.csv`](https://github.com/GeoPressure/GeoLocator-DP/blob/main/example/observations.csv)

fields.name: ring_number
fields.description: Ring number associated with the observed bird. This is the bird-level identifier used to connect observations over time. It is not a strict foreign key because the same `ring_number` can appear in multiple `tags` rows (e.g., multiple deployments on the same bird).

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. `tag_id` is NOT required in this table so that you can enter any relevant ringed species (e.g., control group). Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id). When provided, it should refer to a deployment associated with the same bird (`ring_number`).

fields.name: observation_type
fields.description: Type of observation.

categories.label: Attachment of the tag to the bird. If you equip a new tag at the same time as retrieving an old one from the same bird, create two dedicated rows in the dataset: one for retrieval and one for equipment.

Retrieval of the data, generally through recapture and tag removal, but it can also happen through remote download readout methods (see [`tags.readout_method`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#readout_method)).

General case of capturing a bird while neither deploying nor retrieving a tag. This option covers (1) recapturing a bird without a device (choose `missing` in `device_status`), (2) a capture before `equipment` or after `retrieval`, and (3) captures of individuals from the control group. Recapture/retrap are not hard-coded in the dataset, but inferred from consecutive captures of the same `ring_number`.
Known presence of the bird on a date and location outside ringing (e.g., direct field observation with a color ring).
Any other observation type. Avoid using this; if used, always provide [`observation_comments`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/observations#observation_comments).

fields.name: datetime
fields.description: Date and optionally time of the observation. Accepts any valid [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) date or datetime string, including date-only (`YYYY-MM-DD`), full datetime in local time (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm`), in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ`), or in any specific timezone (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm+hh:mm`).

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: Latitude of the observation location in decimal degrees, using the WGS84 datum.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: Longitude of the observation location in decimal degrees, using the WGS84 datum.

fields.name: location_name
fields.description: Given name of the observation location. It might be helpful to keep a human-readable name of the location to differentiate the location of different observations more easily.

fields.name: device_status
fields.description:
Status of the tag itself (not the data inside the tag).

Can only be `present` for `observation_type` `equipment` or `retrieval`.

categories.label: No tag on the bird and this is expected (e.g., pre-equipment, post-removal, or control group). Only for `observation_type='capture'`.
Tag lost by the bird. Only for `observation_type='capture'`. If a new tag is deployed on a bird that lost its previous tag, create two rows: one `capture`-`missing` and one `equipment`-`present`.

fields.name: observer
fields.description: The name of the individual or group who made the observation.

fields.name: catching_method
fields.description: Catching method according to [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=12). Most records use `M`, `N` or `Z`.

categories.label: Not applicable, the bird was not caught
Trap automatically triggered by the bird
Caught in flight by anything other than a static mist net
Net just under the water surface, lifted as waterfowl swim over it
By hand, with or without hook or noose

fields.name: age_class
fields.description: Life stage of the bird according to the age class in [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=14). The code describes the plumage of the bird rather than its age in years.

categories.label: Pullus: nestling or chick, unable to fly freely

fields.name: sex
fields.description: Sex of the bird according to [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=13).

fields.name: condition
fields.description: Condition of the bird following a simplified version of the [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=23). Assumed to be `alive` if not provided.

categories.label: Found sick, wounded or otherwise unhealthy

fields.name: mass
fields.description: Mass of the tagged bird. See [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=27). Expressed in grams.

fields.name: wing_length
fields.description: Maximum chord measurement. See [EURING Exchange Code](https://euring.org/files/documents/E2020ExchangeCodeV201.pdf#page=26). Expressed in millimeters.

fields.name: additional_metric
fields.description: A list of additional measurements, facts, characteristics, or assertions about the record. Recommended best practice is to use a key:value encoding schema for a data interchange format such as JSON.

fields.name: observation_comments
fields.description: Comments or notes about the observation.

schema.name: measurements
schema.title: Measurements

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: sensor
fields.description: Sensor type.

categories.label: Light-level values measured by a solar geolocator. Range and units may vary by provider and tag settings.

Measure of movement performed by the bird, computed from acceleration sensors. Range and computation method may vary by tag provider, model, settings, and placement on the animal. In general, higher values indicate more activity. Typically computed as the cumulative sum of the absolute difference of acceleration along the z-axis. See [doi:10.1186/s40462-018-0137-1](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40462-018-0137-1) (SOI), [doi:10.1111/jav.01068](https://doi.org/10.1111/jav.01068) (Lund), and the [migratetech report](https://www.migratetech.co.uk/IntigeoSummary.pdf) for more details.

Mean acceleration along the z-axis, computed from acceleration sensors. Mainly used by SOI devices. This metric is sometimes used as a proxy for pitch and was named `pitch` in GeoLocator DP versions earlier than v1.0.
Temperature measured by the tag sensor located between the tag and the animal (body temperature). Units: degrees Celsius.
Temperature measured by the tag sensor pointing outward from the animal (air temperature). This typically corresponds to the main external temperature sensor. Units: degrees Celsius.
Acceleration measured by the tag along the X axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: g (standard gravity, 1 g = 9.80665 m/s^2).
Acceleration measured by the tag along the Y axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: g (standard gravity, 1 g = 9.80665 m/s^2).
Acceleration measured by the tag along the Z axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: g (standard gravity, 1 g = 9.80665 m/s^2).
Magnetic field strength measured by the magnetometer along the X axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: gauss (1 G = 100 microtesla).
Magnetic field strength measured by the magnetometer along the Y axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: gauss (1 G = 100 microtesla).
Magnetic field strength measured by the magnetometer along the Z axis of the forward-right-down frame. Units: gauss (1 G = 100 microtesla).
Wet count during a measurement interval from the wet-dry sensor. Units are usually device-specific.
Conductivity measured by the wet-dry sensor. Unit varies by model.

fields.name: datetime
fields.description: Date and time of the measurement. Accepts any valid [ISO 8601](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) datetime string, including datetime in local time (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm`), in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmZ`) or any specific timezone (`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm+hh:mm`).

fields.name: value
fields.description: Value of the measurement taken by the sensor.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Labeling of pressure and acceleration data according to the [labeling chapter of the GeoPressureManual](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureManual/labelling-tracks.html).

schema.name: staps
schema.title: Stationary periods

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: stap_id
fields.description: Identifier of the stationary period for a given `tag_id`.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Date and time of the start of the stationary period. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Date and time of the end of the stationary period. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: known_lat
fields.description: Latitude of the known stationary period. This value is typically assigned by [`GeoPressureR::tag_set_map()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/tag_set_map).

fields.name: known_lon
fields.description: Longitude of the known stationary period. This value is typically assigned by [`GeoPressureR::tag_set_map()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/tag_set_map).

schema.name: twilights
schema.title: Twilights
schema.description: Table containing twilight data inferred from light data for all tags. Twilight data is typically computed with [`GeoPressureR::twilight_create()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/twilight_create.html).

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: twilight
fields.description: Date and time of the twilight event. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: rise
fields.description: Boolean value to indicate if the twilight is a sunrise (true) or sunset (false).

fields.name: label
fields.description: Labeling of twilight data according to the [GeoPressureManual](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureManual/light-map.html#manual-labelling-of-twilight). The value `discard` indicates that the twilight should not be used for geopositioning. Any other value can be used without affecting the workflow; setting it to `stap_id` typically helps visualize which twilights belong to the same stationary period in the training set.

schema.name: paths
schema.title: Paths
schema.description:
A GeoPressureR `path` contains positions along a bird trajectory.

{:.alert .alert-info}
See [`paths.type`](#type) for the supported trajectory types and how they are created.

`path` should always be used in combination with [`staps`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/staps), joined by the composite key (`tag_id`, `stap_id`).

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type of trajectory.

categories.label: Created with [`tag2path()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/tag2path) from a likelihood map.

fields.name: stap_id
fields.description: Identifier of the stationary period. Together with [`tag_id`](#tag_id), this forms a foreign key to [`staps`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/staps) (`tag_id`, `stap_id`).

fields.name: lat
fields.description: Latitude of the stationary period.

fields.name: lon
fields.description: Longitude of the stationary period.

fields.name: j
fields.description: Trajectory identifier within each combination of `tag_id` and `type`. For `simulation`, use an integer from `1` to `nj` as defined in [`GeoPressureR::graph_simulation()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/graph_simulation). Use `1` for other trajectory types.

schema.name: edges
schema.title: Edges
schema.description: In GeoPressureR, `edges` (graph edges; see more information on the movement model in the [GeoPressureManual](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureManual/trajectory.html)) are used to extract flight information from GeoPressureR [`paths`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/paths) using `path2edge()`.

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: type
fields.description: Same as [`paths.type`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/paths#type).

fields.name: stap_s
fields.description: Identifier of the SOURCE stationary period. Together with [`tag_id`](#tag_id), this forms a foreign key to [`staps`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/staps) (`tag_id`, `stap_id`).

fields.name: stap_t
fields.description: Identifier of the TARGET stationary period. Generally `stap_s+1`; it can be larger when the trajectory skips intermediate stationary periods. Together with [`tag_id`](#tag_id), this forms a foreign key to [`staps`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/staps) (`tag_id`, `stap_id`).

fields.name: lat_s
fields.description: Latitude of the source stationary period.

fields.name: lon_s
fields.description: Longitude of the source stationary period.

fields.name: lat_t
fields.description: Latitude of the target stationary period.

fields.name: lon_t
fields.description: Longitude of the target stationary period.

fields.name: j
fields.description: Trajectory identifier within each combination of `tag_id` and `type`. For `simulation`, use an integer from `1` to `nj` as defined in [`GeoPressureR::graph_simulation()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/graph_simulation). Use `1` for other trajectory types.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Date and time of the start of the flight. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Date and time of the end of the flight. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: n
fields.description: Flight number.

fields.name: distance
fields.description: Distance of the flight in km.

fields.name: bearing
fields.description: Direction of the flight in degrees. 0 indicates north and values increase clockwise. In general, this should be 0°-360°, but -180° to 180° is also allowed.

fields.name: gs_u
fields.description: The average groundspeed of the entire flight along the longitudinal axis (east-west direction), measured in kilometers per hour (km/h).

fields.name: gs_v
fields.description: The average groundspeed of the entire flight along the latitudinal axis (north-south direction), measured in kilometers per hour (km/h).

fields.name: ws_u
fields.description: The average windspeed of the entire flight along the longitudinal axis (east-west direction), measured in kilometers per hour (km/h).

fields.name: ws_v
fields.description: The average windspeed of the entire flight along the latitudinal axis (north-south direction), measured in kilometers per hour (km/h).

schema.name: pressurepaths
schema.title: Pressurepaths
schema.description:
{:.alert .alert-info}
A GeoPressureR `pressurepath` contains ERA5 variables along the bird trajectory at hourly intervals, using the exact bird location (including flight segments). [Read more about pressurepaths in the GeoPressureManual](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureManual/pressurepath.html)

See [`pressurepaths.type`](#type) for the supported trajectory types and how they are created.

`pressurepath` should be used in combination with [`staps`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/staps) and [`paths`](/GeoLocator-DP/geopressurer/paths). For stationary rows, join to `staps` on (`tag_id`, `stap_id`). When joining to `paths`, also match `type` and `j` to keep trajectories separate. Decimal `stap_id` values during flight do not match a stationary-period row in either table.

{:.alert .alert-warning}
Only `tag_id` is defined as a strict foreign key here. `stap_id` can be decimal during migration segments, so it cannot be enforced as a strict foreign key to `staps` in all rows.

The definition below does not list ERA5 variables, which can (and should!) be added to the table as additional columns (e.g., `'altitude'` or `'surface_pressure'`). Read more about these variables in [the documentation of `pressurepath_create()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/pressurepath_create.html#arg-variable).

fields.name: tag_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the tag. Foreign key to [`tags.tag_id`](/GeoLocator-DP/core/tags#tag_id).

fields.name: datetime
fields.description: Date and time of the pressure measurement. Formatted as an ISO 8601 string with timezone designator `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ`.

fields.name: stap_id
fields.description: Identifier of the stationary-period index for the trajectory. Integer values correspond to `staps.stap_id` within the same `tag_id`; decimal values indicate pressure measurements taken during migration between two integer stationary periods. For this reason, `stap_id` is not a strict foreign key in this table.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Type of trajectory.

categories.label: Created with [`tag2path()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/tag2path) from a likelihood map.

fields.name: lat
fields.description: Latitude of the trajectory position at this timestamp.

fields.name: lon
fields.description: Longitude of the trajectory position at this timestamp.

fields.name: j
fields.description: Trajectory identifier within each combination of `tag_id` and `type`. For `simulation`, use an integer from `1` to `nj` as defined in [`GeoPressureR::graph_simulation()`](https://geopressure.org/GeoPressureR/reference/graph_simulation). Use `1` for other trajectory types.
